note: The home chord as a run: Do Mi Sol and the high Do one per beat on a staff with the metronome, then the book's home chord run in eighths with its two chords and then alone. The tempo is moves (40 to 60), so each tool is written at 40 and keeps that distance; the staff can move key, and its line about another key is marked {{?key}}. The high Do is on "oo", and the one care line sits where the passes climb. missing: a run-singer prop that caps the top note (its last pass puts the high Do on the top of the voice's range, so the text says where to stop), and an arpeggio run the book rates under Hard.

exercise.title: The home chord as a quick run
exercise.why: The run skips through Do, Mi, Sol and the high Do, so once each note has its place one per beat, the run only moves between places your voice already knows.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the metronome and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. From the low {{1}}, sing {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}} and on up to the next {{1}}, then come back down the same way, one note per beat. Sing it on the note names.
Practice until each skip lands on its click without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the four notes sit higher or lower, and each skip is still the same distance.

Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run skips from Do up through Mi and Sol to the high Do and back, two notes per beat, and each pass starts a semitone higher. Sing along on "ah", and take the high Do on "oo".
If the high Do feels tight, leave it out and sing the three notes under it.
_Don't reach for high notes: stop singing at the pass where the run stops feeling easy, and listen to the rest._

Press Play below to hear the run: the mic starts with it. The chords are gone now, so you find each new key from the run's first note. Sing along on "ah", and take the high Do on "oo".
If a pass starts off its note, listen to that pass and come in on the next one.
